newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Mergers to strengthen Lithuanian banks - Sharkinas.
newsitem.headline: Mergers to strengthen Lithuanian banks - Sharkinas.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas said on Thursday the country's banking sector will probably be strengthened in 1997 through mergers.
The sector is in the process of recovering from a crisis that broke at the end of 1995 when two of the country's top banks were unexpectedly shut by the central bank.
"I think that very strong banks will appear in 1997, probably when the bigger banks merge," Sharkinas said at a news conference.
"I think that the total number of banks -- 12 commercial, one property and one investment -- will decrease before the end of the year.
"The banking system will become stronger and the international standards of accounting and auditing will show positive results," he added.
Sharkinas said the sector was on the road to recovery after being shaken by the crisis.
"Last year was not easy for the banks after the events of late 1995," he said.
"Confidence in the banks was shattered, but the situation has changed dramatically over the past year and confidence is returning."
Sharkinas said deposits and assets had risen in the sector and foreign investment had grown.
Leading bank Vilniaus Bank is 86 percent foreign-owned, Hermis Bank is 74 percent, and Ukio Bank is 56 percent foreign-owned, Sharkinas said.
"All operating banks have been inspected for the first time, and these inspections will be carried out every year," he said. "All banks have carried out their minimum risk requirements."
